answer: Each agent earns influence only after completing a sequence of paid tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned peers with established stake. A new identity cannot simply forge a reputation: it must lock scarce tokens for each task, and dishonest work risks slashing that stake when peers reveal inconsistent outputs. Spreading attacks across identities multiplies the required capital, while coordination can expose the group’s shared behavior. The haven is costly entry, not anonymity; the trellis of checks makes each false identity an ongoing liability.
